subject: Re: Data guardrails — per-tenant retention & regional storage options
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finedge.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Green <marcus.green@procurecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant-level guardrails: retention windows & regional storage options

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the product demo yesterday — helpful overview. Two follow-ups from our security and procurement teams:

1) We need per-tenant configurable retention (30/90/365 days) with enforced deletion at TTL expiry and a programmatic API to trigger immediate purge for regulated data sets.
2) We must ensure customer data can be pinned to a U.S. geofenced storage region (no cross-border replicas) and we need audit logs for any movement/ejection.

Can Redwood support both in the short term, and if not, what is the earliest roadmap milestone we can expect? Marcus on procurement is copied for SOW/timing constraints.

Attachments: finedge-data-classification.xlsx (customer-side data categories)

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Cloud Security
FinEdge

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finedge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level guardrails: retention windows & regional storage options

Hi Sarah — looping in product and engineering to scope. Short answers: we have primitives today (tenant scoping, region tags), but per-tenant automated TTL enforcement and a self-service purge API are not GA and will need a short roadmap.

Karthik — can you flag any timing/contract constraints from procurement?

Grace/Evelyn — can you take a look at FinEdge's classification (attached) and propose minimal deliverables to meet their ask with the least customer impact? Specifics I think we should address: per-tenant TTL configs, hard delete API, regional storage pinning (no cross-region replicas), and deletion/audit proofs (logs + WORM export).

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finedge.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level guardrails: retention windows & regional storage options

On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 9:12 AM Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finedge.ai> wrote:
> Hi Mina,
>
> Thanks for the product demo yesterday — helpful overview. Two follow-ups from our security and procurement teams: ...

Thanks for the clear ask, Sarah — appreciate the classification table. I sketched a pragmatic roadmap that balances speed and auditability. High level:

- Phase 0 (ASAP, 4–6 wks):
  - Tenant-level TTL config in Console + API (30/90/365 preset + custom numeric days).
  - Soft-delete lifecycle enforcement (mark-for-deletion after TTL, 7-day grace window).
  - Audit events emitted to our tenant audit stream (timestamp, actor, action, resource id).

- Phase 1 (3 months):
  - Hard-delete purge API (idempotent) with job status + requestor trace. For compliance use-cases we will add an asynchronous job to wipe KV cache, object buckets, and index shards.
  - Region pinning controls: storage residency flag per-tenant that prevents creating replicas outside pinned region; initial support: us-central, us-east.

- Phase 2 (4–6 months):
  - Cross-region proof-of-deletion (signed export), KMS key scoping per region, and optional WORM retention windows for regulated subsets.

Open questions for FinEdge to confirm (these will materially affect scope and timeline):
1) Do you require immediate hard-delete with zero grace window for certain categories, or is a short grace acceptable?
2) Should retention be configurable per-tenant only, or per-tenant+dataset (e.g., PII vs. logs)?
3) Any mandatory KMS/HSM provider — do you need separate keys per tenant/region?

I've attached a short proposal PDF that maps these phases to product owners/acceptance criteria and an internal implementation note for engineering. Evelyn — I've put a conservative engineering estimate in the doc; please review and add infra constraints (KV eviction, background sweepers, storage rebalancing).

Links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2b3RetentionGuardrails (proposal draft)
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-7832

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Data Controls
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finedge.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Green <marcus.green@procurecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level guardrails: retention windows & regional storage options

Thanks Grace — this is helpful and the phased plan makes sense. Quick responses to your questions:

1) For regulated PII categories we require hard-delete within 48 hours of request (no grace). For lower-sensitivity logs, a 7-day grace is fine.
2) We need per-tenant+dataset granularity (PII vs. analytics). See the attached classification table for examples.
3) We use AWS KMS and will require per-tenant CMKs scoped to a U.S. account; if Redwood can integrate with customer-managed keys in Phase 1 that would be ideal, otherwise Phase 2 is acceptable.

Procurement note (Marcus): we need an ETA for Phase 0 and Phase 1 to sync SOW. Marcus — can you please confirm target procurement window (we're aiming to include this in a December SOW).

If you can confirm the Phase 0 deliverables and provide an initial timeline by EOW next week, we can proceed to cadence and a statement of work.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Cloud Security, FinEdge
